newsitem.title: UK: UK RETAIL PRICES RISE YR/YR 3.3 PCT IN JULY.
newsitem.headline: UK RETAIL PRICES RISE YR/YR 3.3 PCT IN JULY.

text.p: The Office for National Statistics released the following retail price indices for July:
RETAIL PRICES INDEX JULY JUNE JULY 96
Mth pct change ex MIPs, tax -0.5 0.3 -0.5
COMPONENT DETAILS OF THE ALL-ITEMS INDEX (PCT CHANGES) -
NOTE - Consensus forecast was RPI unchanged MM, +3.1 pct YY RPIX +2.8 pct YY, RPIY +2.3 pct YY
* Highest yr/yr increase in all items RPI since September 1995 when it rose 3.9 percent.
** 0.9 percent annual increase in household goods prices last lower in October 1994.
The ONS said the increase in the all-items 12-month rate was largely due to rises in housing and motoring costs and a further upward effect from seasonal food prices.
A small further upward effect on the 12-month rate came from leisure services which was offset by falling fuel and light charges.
Seasonal food prices fell by 2.9 percent over the month compared with a 9.1 percent fall in July last year.
Housing prices were inflated by a 4.1 percent rise in the mortgage interest payments component. Average mortgage rates rose by about 0.28 percentage points in July.

The 6.4 percent annual rise in motoring costs was due to petrol prices which rose by around 2.5 pence per litre in July. Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown raised duty on petrol by about four pence per litre in his July budget.
Leisure services prices rose on an annual basis as holiday prices were increased more sharply than last year.
The ONS said the overall pattern in clothing and footwear and household goods prices was the same as last year.
The ONS said pork prices may fall in August and cheaper sugar prices, due to a revaluation of the green pound, could cut soft drinks prices and other sugar-based products.
A rise in tea prices is predicted.
For housing prices, most major mortgage lenders raised their lending rates again in August, most by a quarter-point. The effect of last week's base rate rise is not yet quantifiable.
The effect of the mortgage rate rises will be compounded by last August's reductions in lending rates, the ONS said.
The cut in VAT on heating fuel to five percent, from eight, will be felt in September.
Telephone line rental charges will continue to increase up to September.
